analysis:
The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is one added documentation bullet at head line 1025 (patch hunk @@ -1022,6 +1022,7). It says App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice needs a matching fresh coordinator decision, and applies to both doctor summaries. It links ../reference/provider-authorization.md. I examined the supplied base text (lines 1-803 of the file, in two units), which does not include the changed region; the patch excerpt is complete and shows the whole change. Nothing in the diff changes code, protocol, key custody, token handling, cache behavior or authorization logic.

The addition is consistent with T-053 (stale authorization and leases), T-057 (premature MDM removal stranding a provider) and T-058 (diagnostics that misstate trust). It separates lease visibility from removal advice, which is a conservative framing. I found no weakening of a control and no new attack surface. No threat-model update is needed beyond the existing T-053/T-057 coverage.

Unverified contract: the claim that doctor summaries require a fresh coordinator decision before giving MDM removal advice describes code (DoctorCommand, EnrollCommand and the unenroll --keep-serving path) that was not supplied. The linked provider-authorization.md was also not supplied, so it is not verified that the docs match the implementation. This is a documentation accuracy question, not a demonstrated vulnerability. The base text of the cli-reference file also contains an unrelated pre-existing statement about logout and revocation, which I did not treat as new.
